newsitem.title: USA: U.S. swap spreads approaching the vanishing point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. swap spreads approaching the vanishing point.

text.p: Spreads on U.S. interest rate swaps, stuck at historically tight levels for months, broke out of their recent doldrums this week but not in the expected direction.
With dealers in a clump, positioned for spreads to widen, bond issuers have bombarded the market looking for fixed-rate paying deals. Spreads broke out of the range but narrowed.
"Issuers have piled on and crushed five- and 10-year spreads leaving no one wanting to go the other way," one New York based dealer said Thursday.
On 10-year LIBOR swaps, spreads were quoted Thursday at 29 to 30 basis points bid, 31 basis points offered, slightly tighter than Wednesday's quotes.

In addition to bond-related swapping, two other factors also loom large, dealers said. They cited the falling probability of a short-term rate hike from the Fed and expectations for a smooth auction of 10-year notes next month.
"It makes good sense now that spreads are coming in and they could come in another two to three basis points," the head of one swap desk noted.

Spreads generally widen when expectations for forward short-term rates rise or the TED spread widens. That could happen if market participants expected major rate hikes from the Fed, an event considered highly unlikely given current economic trends and data.

A messy 10-year note auction could lead to scarcity in the repurchase market and wider spreads. If 10-year notes go on special, swappers put on cost-of-carry trades, buying bonds on borrowed money and hedging with swaps, that generally push spreads out.

Spreads on swaps longer than 10 years have also narrowed, with 15-year spreads quoted at a midpoint of 49 basis points over the 10-year note and 30-year spreads at 32 basis points over the 30-year bond.

The five-year sector has been hit hard with Eurobond issuers looking to swap as well. Spreads at five years were quoted at 21 basis points bid, 23 to 24 basis points offered, about one basis point tighter than Wednesday.
The short end remained tight on the economic outlook. Spreads on two-year swaps were quoted at 13 to 14 basis points bid, 16 basis points offered, close to Wednesday's levels.
A three-basis-point yield gap between the two-year note auctioned this week and the previous on-the-run issue remained on Thursday, keeping dealer quotes at two years lower than before the auction.
On three-year LIBOR swaps, spreads were quoted at 18 basis points bid, 20 basis points offered, slightly tighter than Wednesday.
